title: Memory leak when shutting down embedded PySide/PyQt4 python code
body_html:
I'm working on a C++ Qt4 application with an embedded python interpreter loading some PySide (or PyQt4) scripts. I noticed that Address Sanitizer was reporting a memory leak on exit c++ exit.

Trying to get to the bottom of this issue, I wrote a simple PySide code embedded in C++ to try to understand where the memory leak was coming from.

I poked around for quite some time trying various things, but to no avail. I suspect that it's linked to some ref-counting error causing some trouble when the Python interpreter shuts down, but I'm not sure.

Could somebody help me understand what I'm doing wrong?

Here is my simple code:

#include <iostream>
#include "Python.h"

class EmbedPySide
{

public:

  EmbedPySide()
  {
    char name[] = "test";
    Py_SetProgramName(name);
    Py_Initialize();

    std::string code =
        "from PySide import QtGui\n"
        ""
        "class EmbededPySide(QtGui.QApplication):\n"
        ""
        "    def __init__(self):\n"
        "        super(EmbededPySide, self).__init__([])\n"
        "        self.button = QtGui.QPushButton('Shutdown')\n"
        "        self.button.clicked.connect(self.cleanUp)\n"
        "        self.win = QtGui.QMainWindow()\n"
        "        self.win.setCentralWidget(self.button)\n"
        "        self.win.move(600, 300)\n"
        "        self.win.show()\n"
        ""
        "    def cleanUp(self):\n"
        "        del self.button\n"
        "        del self.win\n"
        "        self.quit()\n"
        ""
        "if __name__=='__main__':\n"
        "    app = EmbededPySide()\n"
        "    app.exec_()";

    PyRun_SimpleString(code.c_str());
  }

  ~EmbedPySide()
  {
    Py_Finalize();
    std::cout << "Destructor called" << std::endl;
  }

};

int main()
{
  EmbedPySide embedded;

  std::cout << "Exiting" << std::endl;
}

And I compiled it with:

g++ main.cpp -O1 -g -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer \
-I/usr/include/python2.7 -lpython2.7

For clarity, here is the python code I wrote in the code string:

from PySide import QtGui

class EmbededPySide(QtGui.QApplication):

    def __init__(self):
        super(EmbededPySide, self).__init__([])
        self.button = QtGui.QPushButton('Shutdown')
        self.button.clicked.connect(self.cleanUp)
        self.win = QtGui.QMainWindow()
        self.win.setCentralWidget(self.button)
        self.win.move(600, 300)
        self.win.show()

    def cleanUp(self):
        del self.button
        del self.win
        self.quit()

if __name__=='__main__':
    app = EmbededPySide()
    app.exec_()

On run, this is the output I get:

Exiting

Destructor called

================================================================= ==5063==ERROR: LeakSanitizer: detected memory leaks

Direct leak of 3377664 byte(s) in 1228 object(s) allocated from: #0 0x7f161d4fb79a in __interceptor_calloc (/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libasan.so.2+0x9879a) #1 0x7f161d0349ab (/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libpython2.7.so.1.0+0x1619ab)

Direct leak of 786432 byte(s) in 1 object(s) allocated from: #0 0x7f161d4fb79a in __interceptor_calloc (/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libasan.so.2+0x9879a) #1 0x7f161d0349ab (/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libpython2.7.so.1.0+0x1619ab) #2 0x4f622d95dcb87ff ()

Direct leak of 24680 byte(s) in 27 object(s) allocated from: #0 0x7f161d4fb602 in malloc (/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libasan.so.2+0x98602) #1 0x7f161cfacd48 in _PyObject_GC_Malloc (/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libpython2.7.so.1.0+0xd9d48)

[...]

Thank you!

events.body_html: Can you run with export ASAN_OPTIONS=malloc_context_size=20 and install Python dbgsym package (for symbolized stacktrace)?

I'm not familiar with the use of the -dbgsym packages, but if I understood properly, they are found automatically by the system if installed? I ran my program again with export ASAN_OPTIONS[..] enable. The full LeakSanitizer output can be found here: pastebin.ca/4007920
"they are found automatically by the system if installed" - yes, modulo bugs. You might also need to enable Asan address symbolizer as described e.g. here.
It took me some time to be able to get the python debug symbols, but here is the output of my second try: pastebin.com/SK6qCskP
